transcript.text: I've just bought an AEG L7FEE865R and the Eco 40-60 wash says 3:39 and seems to take forever. My old machine did a 40 wash in an hour. Is it faulty? Should I send it back?

## It's almost certainly not faulty

A 3½–4 hour Eco 40-60 cycle is normal for modern machines, including this AEG.

Why it's so long:
• Since 2021, EU and UK energy labelling rules require every machine's energy rating to be measured on its Eco 40-60 programme. It's designed to clean a mixed load of 40°C and 60°C-rated items while using as little energy and water as possible.
• Most of a wash's energy goes on heating water. Eco heats to a lower actual temperature than the "40–60" suggests and makes up for it with longer soaking and tumbling. Detergent has more time to work, so you get a similar clean for much less electricity.
• So the long time is how it achieves its energy rating, not a sign of a problem.

The time may also drop after you start it. The AEG's ProSense system weighs the load in the first few minutes and adjusts. With a half load you'll often see the time come down noticeably.

## If you want a faster wash

• Cottons at 40°C: shorter than Eco, but uses more energy.
• The 20-minute quick programme: good for small, lightly soiled loads (around 3 kg).
• TimeManager or time-reduction button (if your control panel has one): shortens most programmes.

Eco is the cheapest to run, so it's worth using when you're not in a hurry, especially overnight or while you're out. Delay start is handy for this.

## Signs it would actually be faulty

• Error codes on the display (often starting with "E")
• Water not heating, or the drum not draining or spinning
• The cycle running well beyond the displayed time, or the timer stuck
• Clothes coming out still dirty, soaking wet, or smelling bad

If none of those are happening, I wouldn't send it back. If you simply decide you don't like the machine, check the retailer's returns policy. Online purchases in the UK usually come with a 14-day cooling-off period, but that's a change-of-mind return rather than a fault claim.
